post.description: Submit an asynchronous task for background processing. Returns a task ID that you can use to poll for results or receive via webhook.

payload.prompt: What is the weather in New York?

200.description: Task created successfully. Returns task ID and initial status.

409.description: Conflict - Task with this idempotencyKey already exists

429.description: Queue Limit Exceeded - Organization has reached maximum queued tasks

post.description: Submit up to 500 async tasks in one request. Each task is validated independently, so one invalid task does not block the rest. Returns per-task results.

schema.description: Array of task objects to create.

payload.prompt: What do you know about Acme Corp?

200.description: Batch processed. Check the summary and individual results for per-task success or failure.

422.description: Validation Error - Request body is not a valid array or is empty

429.description: Queue Limit Exceeded - The entire batch is rejected because it would exceed your organization's queue capacity

get.description: Poll the status and result of an asynchronous task by ID. Returns the task state and, once complete, the full structured result payload.

parameters.name: taskId

200.description: Successful response with the task status and result if completed.

get.description: Get organization-wide async queue metrics including queued and processing task counts, and concurrency usage.
Returns a list of US states supported for state-level geo-targeting. Only US is currently supported — other country values return an empty array.

citationPills.description: Inline citation pills extracted from the Gemini answer. Each entry is one (pill, source) pair: when a chip cites N sources (Gemini's `+N` analog or section-summary chips), the array contains N entries sharing the same `citationPillId` but with per-source `label`, `url`, and `domain`. Group by `citationPillId` to recover the pill-level structure. `label` is always present on the wire; it can be an empty string when the rail has no title for a source. Omitted from `result` when the answer carries no pills.

label.description: Per-source title from the sources rail (for example `"Quantum computing — Wikipedia"`). Always present on the wire; may be an empty string when the rail has no title for this source — consumers should read `domain` / `url` for source identity in that case.

citationPillId.description: 1-based ordinal shared by all entries from the same chip. Group by `citationPillId` to reconstruct the visible chip; the per-source `label` differs across entries within a chip.

url.description: Direct URL of the cited source.

domain.description: Host extracted from `url`, for grouping and display.

description.description: Source description from the sources rail when Gemini ships one. Omitted when absent.
description.example: Quantum computing is a multidisciplinary field...

position.description: 1-based position of this source in the sibling `result.sources` array.

example.label: Quantum computing — Wikipedia
example.description: Quantum computing is a multidisciplinary field...

model.description: The ChatGPT model used to generate the response

shoppingCards.description: Array of shopping/product cards extracted from the response. The field is omitted entirely from `result` when `include.shopping` is `false` or unset — clients should treat it as optional rather than expecting an empty array.

tags.description: Category tags for the shopping card

position.description: 1-indexed rank across all products in all shopping cards in the response (flat, not reset per card).

inlineProducts.description: Array of inline products with pricing and offers. The field is omitted entirely from `result` when `include.shopping` is `false` or unset — clients should treat it as optional rather than expecting an empty array.

entities.description: Array of entities extracted from the response (when available)

map.description: Array of business/place map entries extracted from the response (when available). Items come from ChatGPT's enriched providers (Yelp, Google Business) and use camelCase field names. The full field set is documented at /api-reference/endpoint/chatgpt/map; only the most commonly populated fields are listed here.

id.description: Business ID (Yelp ID or Google Place ID)

position.description: Position/ranking in results (added by parser)

description.description: Business description
description.example: Specialty coffee roaster known for their meticulous pour-over preparations

example.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
example.description: Specialty coffee roaster known for their meticulous pour-over preparations

citationPills.description: Array of inline citation pills extracted from the response (when available). These are citations that appear inline within the text. Each entry is one (pill, source) pair; group by `citationPillId` to recover pill-level structure.

label.description: Per-source title of the citation. Always present; may be an empty string when the citation event ships no title — read `domain` / `url` for source identity in that case.

description.description: Description of the citation content. Omitted when the citation event carries no snippet (e.g. grouped-webpage title-only cards).
description.example: A detailed description of the cited content

datePublished.description: ISO 8601 date string of when the source was published. Omitted when the citation event carries no publication date.

citationPillId.description: 0-based identifier shared by all entries from the same chip. Group by `citationPillId` to recover the pill-level structure. **Note:** unlike the other providers (Google AIO, AI Mode, Copilot, Perplexity, Gemini) which use 1-based `citationPillId`, ChatGPT's IDs start at 0 for historical reasons.

type.description: Discriminator for the underlying citation event: `searchResult` for inline search citations, `groupedWebpage` for grouped-webpage cards.

position.description: 1-based position of this source in the sibling `result.sources` array.

example.label: Example Article Title
example.description: A detailed description of the cited content

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the error occurred

query.description: The search query to execute on Google

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for localized search results

location.description: Google canonical location name for geo-targeted results, in comma-separated format: 'City,Region,Country' (see https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/data/geotargets for all ~100,000 supported locations). Use alongside 'country' for city-level precision. Mutually exclusive with 'uule' — provide one or the other, not both.

uule.description: Pre-encoded Google UULE string for precise geo-targeting. Use this when you have a pre-built UULE value instead of a location name. Mutually exclusive with 'location' — provide one or the other, not both.

pages.description: Number of search results pages to scrape (1-10)

html.description: Include raw HTML response from Google search

aioverview.description: Include Google AI Overview in the response

markdown.description: Include AI Overview formatted as markdown

paaAioverview.description: Hydrate AI-Overview-type People Also Ask items with markdown content and sources. Costs one extra request per AI-Overview-type PAA item (typically 1-2 per page).

position.description: Position in search results (1-indexed)

displayedLink.description: Formatted URL as displayed in search results

snippet.description: Text snippet describing the page content
snippet.example: Looking for the best programming laptops? We've tested and reviewed the top options...

page.description: Page number this result appeared on (1-indexed)

sitelinks.description: Sitelinks displayed under the main result

peopleAlsoAsk.description: People Also Ask questions from Google

question.example: What specs should I look for in a programming laptop?

snippet.example: Key specifications include RAM, processor, storage, and display quality...

markdown.description: AI Overview markdown content (for AIOVERVIEW type, when include.paaAioverview is true)

sources.description: Cited sources (for AIOVERVIEW type, when include.paaAioverview is true)

description.description: Description of the source

position.description: Position of source (1-indexed)

peopleAreSaying.description: Cards from Google's "What people are saying" / "Trending posts and discussions" SERP module. The field is omitted from `result` when no such module appears on the SERP, so clients should treat it as optional rather than expecting an empty array.

position.description: Position within the module (1-indexed)

title.description: Card title as displayed on the SERP
title.example: Best running shoes 2026 - what runners are saying

link.description: Destination URL the card points to (often a Reddit, Quora, or community forum thread)

date.description: Google's raw relative-time text (e.g., "5 days ago", "2 weeks ago"). Free-form string — not normalized to a timestamp.

localResults.description: Places from Google's local pack (the map-backed "3-pack" of local businesses on local-intent queries, e.g. "best pizza in new york city"). The field is omitted from `result` when no local pack appears on the SERP, so clients should treat it as optional rather than expecting an empty array. Desktop only; mobile and the separate hotels/travel pack are not surfaced.

position.description: Position within the pack (1-indexed)

title.description: Business name as displayed on the SERP

placeId.description: Google entity id for the place

reviews.description: Review count as displayed by Google (e.g. "26K"). Free-form string — not normalized to a number.

price.description: Price band as displayed by Google (e.g. "$10–20"). Currency symbol matches the locale.

yearsInBusiness.description: Years-in-business badge, when shown (typical on service-style packs)

address.description: Street address or locality as displayed on the SERP

hours.description: Opening-hours text as displayed (e.g. "Open · Closes 11 PM", "Open 24 hours")

description.description: Trailing snippet — a review quote or a service-options line
description.example: "Fast service, great atmosphere, and truly scrumptious pizza."

links.description: Action links rendered on the place, typically on business/service-style packs (plumbers, salons, …) and absent on restaurant packs whose places are plain buttons. Each key is present only when Google rendered that button.

localResultsMoreLink.description: Absolute URL of the local pack's "More places" / "More businesses" control — Google's expanded Local Finder for the query. Returned only alongside `localResults` when the SERP renders the control.

link.description: Google search URL for the related query

ads.description: Sponsored ad results from Google search, including text ads (`type: RESULT`) and shopping-style sponsored cards (`type: SHOPPING_CARD`) from the right-hand-side and top-of-page carousels.

position.description: Position within the ad block (1-indexed)

blockPosition.description: Where the ad appeared on the SERP. `top`/`bottom` are text-ad blocks, `middle` covers direct/in-content ads, `rhs` is the right-hand-side sponsored-products carousel.

type.description: Discriminates plain text ads (`RESULT`) from shopping-style sponsored cards (`SHOPPING_CARD`). Shopping cards appear in the right-hand-side PLA carousel, the top-of-page PLA carousel, and the top-of-page sponsored shopping-card carousels (vehicles, products, hotels, …).

url.description: Destination URL of the ad. For `type: SHOPPING_CARD` items this is a Google `aclk?`-redirected URL.

page.description: Page number where the ad was found

displayedUrl.description: Formatted URL as displayed in the ad

description.description: Ad description text. For `type: RESULT` items this is classic ad copy. For `type: SHOPPING_CARD` items it carries category-specific subtitle fragments joined with `·` (e.g. vehicle condition + city: `Used - 94k miles · Greeley`).
description.example: Shop our selection of programming laptops with fast shipping.

category.description: Carousel header label for shopping-card ads. Examples observed today include `Sponsored products`, `Sponsored vehicles`, and `Sponsored hotels`. Omitted for `type: RESULT` text ads.

price.description: Product price for `type: SHOPPING_CARD` ads. `value` and `currency` are populated only when the visible price string parses unambiguously into a number + symbol. `raw` carries the visible text verbatim (e.g. `"$0 down with 24 monthly payments"` on installment offers) so consumers can disambiguate genuine zero prices from down-payment labels.

oldPrice.description: Original price before discount on `type: SHOPPING_CARD` ads that surface MSRP / sale messaging. Same shape as `price`.

store.description: Merchant/dealer name attached to a `type: SHOPPING_CARD` ad.

imageUrl.description: Hero image URL served by Google's `encrypted-tbn` CDN for `type: SHOPPING_CARD` ads. Omitted when the lazy-image chain cannot resolve a non-placeholder source.

description.description: Sitelink description
description.example: High-performance laptops for gaming

aioverview.description: Google AI Overview data (if requested). Returns null when AI Overview is not available after retries.

sources.description: Sources referenced in the AI Overview

position.description: 1-based position index of the source

label.description: Source title (the display label Google renders on the source rail)

description.description: Source description / snippet
description.example: Comprehensive guide to choosing the perfect laptop for software development

citationPills.description: Inline citation pills extracted from the AI Overview answer. Each entry is one (pill, source) pair: when a pill cites N sources (Google's `[Label +N]` chips), the array contains N entries sharing the same `citationPillId` but carrying per-source `label`, `url`, and `domain`. Group by `citationPillId` to recover the pill-level structure. Omitted from `result.aioverview` when the answer carries no pills.

label.description: Per-source title from the sources rail (for example `"Chase Personal Credit Cards"`). Empty string when the rail has no title for this source — consumers should read `domain` / `url` for source identity in that case. Entries grouped under the same `citationPillId` carry different per-source labels.

citationPillId.description: 1-based ordinal shared by all entries from the same chip. Group by `citationPillId` to reconstruct the visible chip; the per-source `label` differs across entries within a chip.

url.description: Direct URL of the cited source.

domain.description: Host extracted from `url`, for grouping and display.

description.description: Source description from the sources rail when Google ships one. Omitted when the source carries no snippet.
description.example: Personal credit cards from Chase.

position.description: 1-based position of this source in the sibling `result.aioverview.sources` array.

relatedLinks.description: A citation chip's "View related links" flyout items — URLs Google groups under the chip that are NOT in the `sources` rail (for example a Google Shopping comparison link). Each entry shares the `citationPillId` of its chip so it can be grouped with that chip's `citationPills`, but carries no `position` (a related link is absent from `sources`). Related links also render inline in `markdown`, so `markdown` may contain more URLs than `sources` / `citationPills` — the extras are accounted for here. Omitted from `result.aioverview` when no chip carries related links.

label.description: The related page's own title. Empty string when Google ships none — read `domain` / `url` for identity in that case.

citationPillId.description: Matches the `citationPillId` of the chip's `citationPills` entries, so a related link can be grouped with its pill.

url.description: Direct URL of the related link.

domain.description: Host extracted from `url`, for grouping and display.

description.description: Snippet Google ships for the related link. Omitted when absent.
description.example: Shop and compare laptops for developers.

text.example: Based on current information, the best laptops for programming typically include models from Apple MacBook Pro, Dell XPS, and Lenovo ThinkPad series...

markdown.description: AI Overview content formatted as markdown (if requested)
markdown.example: Based on current information, the best laptops for programming typically include models from Apple MacBook Pro, Dell XPS, and Lenovo ThinkPad series...

type.description: Sub-type discriminator. TEXT ads carry `domain` + `description`; SHOPPING ads carry `price` + `store` (+ optional `old_price`). Always present.

domain.description: Domain name of the advertiser (present when `type` is `TEXT`)

description.description: Ad description text (present when `type` is `TEXT`)

price.description: Product price (present when `type` is `SHOPPING`). `value` and `currency` are populated only when the visible price string parses unambiguously into a number + symbol; `raw` carries the visible text verbatim.

old_price.description: Original price before discount (present when `type` is `SHOPPING` and the ad has sale pricing). Same shape as `price`.

image.description: Ad image URL (product photo for shopping ads, hero image for text ads)

shoppingCards.description: Shopping product cards extracted from the SERP's organic shopping grids ("Popular products" / "More products"). The field is omitted from `result` when no shopping section is present, so clients should treat it as optional rather than expecting an empty array. Wire shape borrows fields from AI Mode's `shopping_cards` for cross-API familiarity but uses camelCase keys (`productLink`, `oldPrice`) emitted by the Google mapper.

position.description: 1-indexed rank across the whole `shoppingCards` array in DOM order (flat, does not reset per `category` section).

productLink.description: Direct product URL. Click destinations are JS-hydrated, so this is usually an empty string in the static HTML response — the card opens a Google-side sidebar overlay rather than navigating externally.

category.description: Parent section header text. Lets callers distinguish cards from coexisting shopping panels on the same SERP. Current Google-emitted values include "Popular products" and "More products".

price.description: Structured pricing information. `value` and `currency` are populated only when the visible price string parses unambiguously into a number + symbol; `raw` carries the visible text verbatim.

oldPrice.description: Original price before discount. Same shape as `price`.

citationPills.description: Inline citation pills extracted from the Copilot answer. Each entry is one (pill, source) pair: when a pill cites N sources (consecutive citation events grouped into a single chip), the array contains N entries sharing the same `citationPillId` but carrying per-source `label`, `url`, and `domain`. Group by `citationPillId` to recover the pill-level structure. Omitted from `result` when the answer carries no pills.

label.description: Per-source title from the citation event (e.g. `"Microsoft 365 Documentation"`, `"Productivity Best Practices"`). Always present; may be an empty string when the event ships no title — read `domain` / `url` for source identity in that case. Entries grouped under the same `citationPillId` carry different per-source labels.

citationPillId.description: 1-based ordinal shared by all entries from the same chip. Group by `citationPillId` to reconstruct the visible chip; the per-source `label` differs across entries within a chip.

url.description: Direct URL of the cited source.

domain.description: Host extracted from `url`, for grouping and display.

description.description: Source description from the sources rail when Copilot ships one. Omitted when absent.
